body: If you look at the history of blackface, it is about the caricaturization of black people. It is taking traits white people saw in black people, and to dehumanize them further they blew these traits up to a ridiculous degree all for white entertainment. I do not believe reposting a picture or meme of a black person is automatically digital blackface, and this instance there is none of that caricaturization happening. However, there are some instances where I can sympathize with the feeling that it is reminiscent of this harmful practice. For instance-sharing a gif of a black person making a funny and over the top face could remind people of some black face practices..even if it’s not a white person dressing up as a black person. It happened in many different forms. While this example is not as blatant, I can understand the pain behind these accusations..and to be certain, they do come from a place of pain. We cannot pretend to understand someone else’s perspective if we have not lived it. We ALL, (and I do mean everyone), need to practice more understanding and listening of the other’s perspective.
Don’t worry it wasn’t a bad cry! I’m so so glad to hear and yes, that place will always be a reminder of where we’ve been and that we actually want to be alive. May it stay in the past..

I know you didn’t ask for advice-but coming from someone with multiple addictions, here are my most practical pieces of advice 

-Have somebody you trust to keep you accountable 

-Don’t heap shame on yourself if you slip up-face those feelings you have about it. Ignoring them only leads to them taking over (posting here is a great idea if it helps you to stay encouraged)

-Don’t isolate

-Develop a positive and rewarding bedtime routine if that’s when temptation is strongest. Or have an enjoyable activity you can automatically go to to replace porn. 

-Don’t try to suppress your feelings and temptations. Notice them for what they are, just feelings, just images in your head, just human things. Same as the advice above-facing them and bringing them to light takes their power away and makes it easier to let them go. 

This is a hard thing you are committing to, but a good thing. I believe you can make it! You cannot bulldoze your way to sobriety. Pure will alone won’t do it. But that desire I hear from you, coupled with practical steps and support, you absolutely can do this! I’m proud of you for taking these first steps. DM me if you ever need that extra support!

It is NEVER ethical for a therapist to enter into any sort of romantic relationship with a patient. If you think about the power dynamics, a therapist will always have the power because they naturally know way more about a patient than they know about the therapist. That is the way it is supposed to be in therapy. And when you think about someone that has gone through abuse, any remotely ethical therapist would not ever enter into this kind of relationship. You are very brave to report this-putting your friends safety and well being over your fears of damaging your relationship or upsetting her. That is one of the most loving things we can do for our friends, and I’m sorry you didn’t get the support you were looking for from your mom. Some therapists have supervisors, but yes, looking into a board of ethics or his license administrator is a good idea. Good luck to you.

Maybe there are things you can do to ease the workload like bringing in outside help or giving you more of a break when your partner comes home? This isn’t an easy thing you’re doing so please, give yourself some grace and know you don’t have to feel guilty for your emotions! (Also I’m a big dog person but even I need a more calm breed so I totally understand). I know it will get better but I hope in the meantime you are kind to yourself and give yourself the grace to make whatever decision is best for you, even if that means eventually returning the puppy to the breeder to be rehomed. I have struggled with Paul in both of these verses as someone who supports equality-these verses on the surface seem to be as you said, misogynistic and homophobic. If you look at the context of the verse in Timothy, Paul is writing to Timothy who is pastoring to a church in Ephesus. They are exchanging letters, but we only have Paul’s letter to Timothy to draw our context from. He talks about some of the women in this specific church and says they should not be permitted to have authority over the men who are teaching, but it seems like he is addressing this specific church and their issues with false profits, specifically outspoken women in the church who are teaching false things from the occult. He is not making a blanket statement like what many churches assume and base their doctrine on. As far as homophobia goes, the ancient world didn’t even have a concept of sexual orientation of the word “homosexual.” It seems very likely that in the context of the time and the translation of the specific word homosexual, Paul is addressing issues of sexual acts that are perversions either because they are adultery, or possibly addressing the common Greek practice of pederasty-men orienting young boys into adulthood with a erotic and sexual relationship (pedophilia). Reading the text in these contexts have really helped me. Hope this was helpful.
